commit_subject: fix: gate ordinary SECA tax outputs
description: Its ordinary-case section 1401(c) boundary is enforced by the required `no_foreign_system_exclusive_se_income` attestation, exposed as `self_employment_tax_pipeline_domain_is_valid`. When that Judgment is `not_holds`, all three public tax outputs fail closed to zero while the pre-relief income outputs remain observable.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module computed and published the full section 1401(a) and 1401(b)(1) self-employment taxes for every taxpayer with no representation of section 1401(c), which exempts self-employment income that is subject exclusively to a foreign social-security system under a section 233 agreement, so an in-scope exempt taxpayer received a positive SECA tax the statute says is exempt.
triage.triage_notes: Provision was read through the pinned corpus release (resolve_provision.py, us/statute/26/1401): subsection (c) 'Relief from taxes in cases covered by certain international agreements' is present and the module's new proof-atom excerpt is verbatim from it. Pre-fix evidence that the clause was unrepresented rather than merely undocumented: at parent f2aea3b2dc the only mentions of 1401(c) were (a) the module summary saying the executable slice 'assumes ... no section 1401(c) foreign-exclusive social security coverage' and (b) a deferred_outputs entry for us:statutes/26/1401#self_employment_tax_after_international_agreement_exemption; the three public tax formulas were unconditional sum_where/addition expressions. The fix is a single coherent change (one new Judgment rule, one new required Boolean input, three formula gates, summary rewrite) with no unrelated formula, parameter, rate, base, or effective-date changes — the $184,500 base, 0.9235 factor, 12.4%/2.9% rates and 2026-01-01/2026-12-31 windows are untouched. Caveat for a reviewer: the remedy is a conservative fail-closed zero for the whole tax unit, whereas 1401(c) exempts only 'to the extent' the income is subject exclusively to the foreign system; the commit's own summary and the PR body acknowledge the actual foreign-agreement relief calculation remains a deferred boundary, so this corrects a fail-open defect without fully encoding the clause's partial-exemption arithmetic. Commit message is terse ('fix: gate ordinary SECA tax outputs') but PROGRESS.md in the same commit states 'Gated the existing OASDI, hospital-insurance, and combined ordinary SECA tax outputs behind that Judgment without renaming any existing surface', and the PR body (#1003) says '§1401(c) attestation gates the public outputs'. The companion test file adds `seca-foreign-system-boundary-fails-closed` asserting domain_is_valid: not_holds, federal_self_employment_income '46175' still observable, and all three taxes '0'. The new import proof atoms carry hash: sha256:local, and PROGRESS.md lists 'Refresh the downstream SE import hash' as remaining work, so a follow-up commit on the same branch likely rewrites those hashes (mechanical).
triage.verifier_justification: The first reader's premise — "no representation of section 1401(c)" — is factually wrong: the pre-fix module already carried a structured `deferred_outputs` entry `us:statutes/26/1401#self_employment_tax_after_international_agreement_exemption` whose reason names section 1401(c) and states the submodules "do not encode that exemption," and that entry survives this commit verbatim. The fix does not encode the exemption either; it adds a required TaxUnit attestation plus a fail-closed gate, and its own added comment still calls the relief calculation a deferred boundary, so the in-domain encoded meaning is unchanged and the out-of-domain output (zero for the whole tax unit) is not the statutory result for the "to the extent that" partial-exemption case the pinned §1401(c) text actually states. Against that, the pre-fix module did publish a positive `federal_self_employment_tax` for a population the statute exempts with no input by which a caller could express the fact, and the commit adds a breaking required input and a companion showing 7,064.775 → 0, which reads as a genuine fail-open correction. The message is generic ("fix: gate ordinary SECA tax outputs") and the diff is a domain guard rather than a clause encoding, so the evidence does not settle fidelity-correction versus enforcement of an already-declared deferred boundary.
triage.verifier_quote: When that Judgment is `not_holds`, all three public tax outputs fail closed to zero while the pre-relief income outputs remain observable. The unresolved foreign-agreement relief calculation, full upstream section 1402(a) completed-return construction, and the complete cross-referenced wage definition remain explicit deferred boundaries below.
triage.verifier_notes:
Refutation attempt on the KIND failed: if this is kept as fidelity, `unrepresented_clause` is still the best fit. `polarity_or_logic` is tempting because its definition names "fail-open vs fail-closed" and PROGRESS.md calls this "the ordinary SECA fail-closed foreign-coverage boundary," but there was no prior boolean or branch on this condition to invert — the fix creates the branch — so "clause missing, fix adds it" describes it better.

Refutation on the CLASSIFICATION has real force, which is why I land on unclear rather than confirmed:
1. Pre-declared boundary. Pre-fix `deferred_outputs` (unchanged by this commit) reads: "Section 1401(c) exempts income subject exclusively to a foreign social security system under a section 233 agreement. The cap-aware, Person-level section 1401(a) and (b)(1) submodules do not encode that exemption..." Pre-fix summary prose: "The executable slice assumes ... no section 1401(c) foreign-exclusive social security coverage. Those mechanisms ... remain explicit deferred boundaries below." This is scope the module explicitly disclaimed, in machine-readable metadata, not a silent omission.
2. The fix adds no statutory computation. The 1401(c) deferred_outputs entry is byte-identical post-fix; the new rule is a Judgment over a caller attestation, not the exemption.
3. Post-fix is also not source-faithful for the partial case. Pinned §1401(c) (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, provision sha256 38a25e0d...) exempts SE income "to the extent that" it is subject exclusively to the foreign system. The new input `no_foreign_system_exclusive_se_income` is Boolean and TaxUnit-level, while the statutory exemption is per-individual and proportional, so a partially-covered filer now gets zero for the whole unit — wrong in the opposite direction. Zero here is a refusal sentinel, not a computed result.

Counterweights a reviewer should hold against the above, if they want to keep it as confirmed/unrepresented_clause: the pre-fix public output was unconditional over all TaxUnits, `us/statute/26/1401` was a claimed `corpus_citation_paths` entry, the new proof atom is `kind: exception` quoting the §1401(c) text verbatim from the pinned corpus (verified — the excerpt matches the release text exactly), the commit is labeled "fix:", and it adds a *required* input (a breaking caller-contract change), which implies the authors judged the prior surface wrong rather than merely incomplete. New companion `seca-foreign-system-boundary-fails-closed` pins the behavior change: pre-fix would have produced 5,725.70 + 1,339.075 = 7,064.775; post-fix all three tax outputs are '0' with `federal_self_employment_income` still '46175'.

PR #1003 body describes this as the house pattern rather than a one-off correction ("valid ONLY in its verified domain ... out-of-domain fails closed"), applied to the NIIT pipeline in the same PR; if the benchmark wants genuine statutory-meaning defects rather than domain-guard hardening, this case and its NIIT sibling should be judged the same way.
